import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 985

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/985](https://www.erdosproblems.com/985)
-/

namespace Erdos985

/--
Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_985 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp_prime : p.Prime) (hp_nontrivial : p ≠ 2),
    ∃ q, q.Prime ∧ q < p ∧ orderOf (q : ZMod p) = p - 1 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Artin conjectured that 2 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$, which
-- Hooley proved assuming the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

/--
Heath-Brown proved that at least one of 2, 3, or 5 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_985.variants.two_three_five_primitive_root :
    Set.Infinite
      {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧
      (orderOf (2 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨
       orderOf (3 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨
       orderOf (5 : ZMod p) = p - 1)} := by
  sorry

end Erdos985

findings.description: The docstring says “for every prime p,” but the theorem explicitly assumes `hp_nontrivial : p ≠ 2`. This necessary exceptional-case restriction should be documented: there is no prime q < 2, and allowing q = 2 does not help because its residue has multiplicative order 0, not 1. The Lean restriction is appropriate for the intended open problem; this is a documentation issue, not a substantive misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/985 and its LaTeX source say “for every prime p ... a prime q < p.” Erdős's original 1965 article, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-17.pdf, PDF page 39, likewise asks whether “to every p there is a prime q < p which is a primitive root of p,” leaving the evident p = 2 exception implicit.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “for every odd prime p” (or “for every prime p > 2”), and explicitly explain the exclusion of p = 2. Retain the theorem's `p ≠ 2` hypothesis.

reformulations.difference: The primitive-root condition is expressed using `orderOf` in the ring `ZMod p`, rather than explicitly requiring a generator of its multiplicative group of units.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, p − 1 is positive. Thus the asserted order forces the residue of q to be a unit. Its order in the unit group equals its order in the ring's multiplicative monoid. The unit group has cardinality φ(p) = p − 1, so having that order is equivalent to generating the entire unit group. The exact equivalence with existence of a unit representing q whose generated subgroup is ⊤ was proved as `Review985.order_iff_unit_generator` in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The source says that one fixed member of {2,3,5} is a primitive root for infinitely many primes. Lean instead asserts infinitude of primes for which at least one of the three is a primitive root, placing the disjunction inside the set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing S_a for the primes modulo which a is a primitive root, Lean asserts that S_2 ∪ S_3 ∪ S_5 is infinite. A finite union is infinite exactly when at least one constituent is infinite. Hence this is equivalent to ∃ a ∈ {2,3,5}, S_a.Infinite. This exact equivalence was proved as `Review985.heathBrown_iff_fixed_base`.

sources_consulted: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-17.pdf — P. Erdős, Some recent advances and current problems in number theory (1965), especially PDF pages 37–39
https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9807104 — Greg Martin, The Least Prime Primitive Root and the Shifted Sieve, LaTeX introduction
review.notes: No substantive mathematical misformalizations or stale statuses found. The main source still records the problem as open and attributes the solved variant to Heath-Brown. The source's implicit p = 2 exception is not an equivalence with its literal all-primes wording; retaining the Lean exclusion is the appropriate nontrivial interpretation. The docstring's q ≤ p versus Lean's q < p is harmless: equality gives the zero residue, which cannot have order p − 1 for prime p; this was proved in Lean. Definitions, answer scope, quantifiers, and boundary cases were checked. A computational test, proved equivalent to the order criterion for p > 1, found witnesses for every odd prime below 101 and none for p = 2. All scratch experiments compile successfully in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the named equivalence proofs use no sorry. Source pages blocked by Cloudflare were read through r.jina.ai. No repository files were edited.
